newsitem.title: USA: FPC still has no Crystal River nuke restart.
newsitem.headline: FPC still has no Crystal River nuke restart.

text.p: Florida Power Corp (FPC) said it still did not set a restart date for the 825 megawatt (MW) Crystal River nuclear power plant despite a report showing that it would return to service in January 1997.
"The company has not released a date. We don't know when we'll restart," said company spokeswoman Melodye Hendrix.

Today's Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) daily status report showed for the first time a possible startup schedule for the Red Level, Fla., facility that was shut Sept 2 to replace a leaky section of a lubrication oil line.
Industry sources said plant operators usually submit the most "optimistic", not necessarily the most "probable," restart dates to the NRC for its daily status report.
Although repairs to the line were completed at end of September, restart of Crystal River remained off line.
Ahead of a restart, FPC needs to submit safety assessment to the NRC about recent modification on an emergency diesel generator at Crystal River, while NRC must review those data.
"Nothing has been submitted," Hendrix said, but could not provide a time table when the findings could be sent to NRC.
FPC, a subsidiary of Florida Progress Corp, is the operator and majority owner of Crystal River. Ten Florida municipal utilities own the remaining interests in the plant.
